descriptionHtml:
Approach · TC-20 Rounding Dashboard · S04b Nursing Home: the In Today residents fall into the right buckets, with the right unit and open-task count per row

UAT steps / ticket ACs covered:

  • U1 With patients in a mix of pending / in-progress / complete states, the dashboard counts (Total, Pending, In Progress, Complete) match the real patient-list state, in Hospital and in Nursing Home (UAT TC-20; TFA-92598 AC 3) — gate: blocked: TFA-92598 in progress
  • U2 The dashboard is present (reachable from the patient list) and correct in both Hospital and Nursing Home (UAT TC-20; TFA-92598 AC 5) — gate: blocked: TFA-92598 in progress
  • T3 The app counts every patient in Total and in exactly one of Pending (not yet prepped), In Progress and Complete, and shows the counts prominently (TFA-92598 How it works 1; TFA-92598 How it works 2) — gate: blocked: TFA-92598 in progress

Test design technique: Decision table (decision-table) — List the combinations of several conditions and check each one, to see that the result follows the rule.

Given The S04a census (same seed)

When Open the Nursing Home dashboard from the bottom nav

Then Pending 2, In Progress 2, Complete 1, Total 5, counted on the In Today set only; the tiles add up. N1's row reads 'Cedar 101 · 2 tasks pending' and N3's 'Cedar 103 · 1 task pending'. The foreign resident is absent

Pass rule (oracle, excerpt): Ticket rule 1 applied to the In Today set (TFA-92598 AC 4): counts 5/2/2/1 and countsSumToTotal. This catches a Total taken from In Today while the buckets still count every resident. The row lines tie the stored unit and the open-task count to the row (prototype row shape, T2). …

Where it ran: datasets (seeded data sets, list checks) on dev; test method PW · Playwright script; lane planned in the matrix: browser agent (blocked)

S04b is our own case number (its number in the coverage matrix cases/TC-20.matrix.json; a letter suffix = one case split in several), not a step number of the UAT document.
